title: Quad-layout global grid map stage: 1.9 s to under 100 ms
description:
Make the `global grid map` stage of QuadLayoutEngine fast. It takes 1.897 s today. The startup CPU profile's top Java self time is here: ojAlgo AXPY.invoke (8.8% of all samples), GridMapOptimizer.accumulateTriangleRange, maximumStepOfRange, energyOfTriangleRange, SymmetricDirichletEnergy.composeMajorizedHessian. Related: PATCH-40. Baseline, measured 2026-10-15 with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --property quadLayoutScene.alpha=15` on the default model (headless, 9.1 s to ready): cross field 0.395 s, seamless 0.800 s, motorcycle graph 0.145 s, quantization 1.526 s, carve 0.674 s, contract 1.475 s, global grid map 1.897 s. These run synchronously before the scene's first frame, so together they are almost all of the quad-layout scene's time to first paint. The user's goal is first paint under 0.1 s; a sibling ticket moves the pipeline off the first frame, and each stage ticket makes one stage as fast as it can go. Target: this stage under 100 ms on the default model, or as close as the algorithm allows, with the reason it can go no lower. The stage's output must not change: same singularity count, arc/node/patch counts, quad count and a screenshot that image-diffs clean against the master baseline. Use the stage's own `[quad-layout] <stage>` log line and an async-profiler capture (`run-scene --profile`, read with `ixdar-cli profile-report`). Stay inside this stage's package; touch shared code (solver/, HalfEdgeMesh, QuadLayoutEngine) only where the stage needs it, and list every shared-file change in the report, because six sibling tickets run in parallel. Related: CRAW-2 (scan-scale pipeline), CRAW-4 (cached layouts).

Round 2 (user request 2026-10-15). Round 1 is committed in the worktree as 644ac7c5 (output-identical, botijo 1.89 -> 1.59 s, buddha 22.1 -> 16.7 s median). Research findings (web + papers): the reference pipeline is not faster -- Lyon 2021 defers this stage to LCBK19 Section 6.2 (Tutte map per patch to its quantised rectangle, then a global Newton with SLIM/CM, 7.9 s for 39k triangles single-threaded; https://cgg.unibe.ch/media/papers/1269/a51-lyon.pdf). Heuschling 2026 optimises node/arc positions, not this stage. With one refactor ~13 ms vs one solve ~5 ms, stale-factor PCG/inexact Newton cannot win; the route to 5-10x is fewer iterations and smaller/parallel problems. Ranked: (1) per-patch decomposition solved in parallel -- exact if layout arcs stay pinned to rectangle edges, otherwise per-patch solves plus a small interface solve (block Gauss-Seidel or Schur complement); (2) a better flip-free start (convex-combination/Floater mean-value weights computed on the seamless map F's triangles instead of uniform Tutte) plus a BCQN-style characteristic-gradient-norm stopping test (Zhu, Bridson, Kaufman 2018, MIT, http://www.cs.columbia.edu/~kaufman/BCQN/BCQN.html), estimated 32 -> 12-20 iterations; (3) Progressive Parameterizations (Liu et al. 2018, http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~fuxm/projects/ProgressivePara/) reference schedule on top of the existing CM Newton if the start stays highly distorted. Side experiment: analytic eigensystem / absolute-value projection (Smith, De Goes, Kim 2019; Chen et al. 2024), 0-30%. Rejected: SLIM (libigl MPL-2.0, standalone repo GPL-3.0 -- do not read), AQP, AKVF, TLC/lifted energies, GPU. Scaling anomaly to explain first: buddha has ~7x botijo's triangles but takes 15-25x longer.
definition-of-done:
1. The stage's `[quad-layout] global grid map` time on the default quad-layout model is recorded before and after (median of 3 runs) in changes-made, with the after time under 100 ms or a stated reason it cannot be. 2. Singularity count, arc/node/patch counts and quad count match master exactly. 3. A screenshot of the final layout under tmp/ image-diffs clean against a master screenshot taken the same way. 4. No debugging scaffolding is left behind; `ixd wt done` passes.

5. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/<ticket> --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` covers sphere_base, sphere_random, bolt, hand, fandisk, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, Hand-tri-30k, rockerarm, buddha and the crawfish scan (~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, 8 GB heap). Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.

Round 2: the scaling measurement (per-iteration log on botijo and buddha, fill-in, iteration count) is recorded before any method change. Round 2 changes the output in the last bits, so equality is relaxed to: identical singularity, node/arc/patch and quad counts on every suite mesh, every map flip-free, the final distortion energy no worse than master's by more than 0.5% per mesh (reported per mesh), and the max uv deviation from master reported per mesh. Any count change or energy regression stops for a user ruling. Stage time per suite mesh before/after, with botijo and buddha as interleaved medians of 3, goes in changes-made.
testing-plan: 1. On master: run-scene quad-layout three times, record the stage time and counts, take a screenshot. 2. In the worktree: the same three runs plus a profile capture; compare times and counts. 3. image-diff the two screenshots. 4. mvn test for the touched packages.
unknowns: Whether the stage can reach 100 ms without changing its output; if not, what the floor is and why
changes-made: Relaunch progress: master baseline (0f52d26f snapshot, 3 runs, loaded machine): stage 3.357/2.109/3.961 s, uv hash ec1d76ee66e84dbd, singularities 72, nodes/arcs/patches 446/908/454, quads 14444, screenshot sha 22e54fa9. Worktree partial diff (CSR sparsity build, touched-index reduction, parallel patch maps, Newton solve without fold pass) reproduces the master uv hash. Stage split on the worktree: assembly ~0.35-0.65 s (patch maps 0.2-0.4), Newton ~1.1-1.5 s (32 iterations: AMD ordering 0.11-0.23 s + first factor 0.05-0.1 s, 31 PARDISO refactors ~0.35-0.5 s, solves ~0.15-0.2 s, assembly ~0.2 s), extraction ~0.2 s. Finding: the MKL thread count changes PARDISO's bits on the 44k-variable Newton system (4 threads gave uv hash 481a5865), so refactor threading cannot be tuned without changing output.

A/B interleaved, 3 runs each under the suite jvm.lock, botijo alpha=15: master global grid map 1.877/1.937/1.888 s (median 1.888 s), worktree 1.687/1.499/1.586 s (median 1.586 s, -16%). Every run: uv hash ec1d76ee66e84dbd, rectangle hash 821184558ef751c7, energy 42151.48787630567, singularities 72, nodes/arcs/patches 446/908/454, quads 14444, screenshot sha256 22e54fa9... identical (byte-identical PNG). Added: GridMapIsoSurface face lookup is an int array instead of a HashMap<Integer,Integer> (u/v are called ~30 times per trace step in extraction). Tried and dropped: parallel port tracing in QuadMeshExtraction (no gain, 2x work), single-threaded MKL for patch maps (risk of bit changes on bigger patches), fewer MKL threads for the Newton refactor (changes bits), single-threaded PARDISO solve phase (breaks the next refactor with a zero pivot).

Relaunch 2 (floor measurement): temporary per-phase timing on botijo (removed again; NewtonRelaxation and QuadLayoutEngine back to the pre-instrumentation state) gives stage 1.48-1.58 s = assembly 0.30 s + Newton 1.04-1.12 s + extraction 0.13-0.16 s. Inside Newton: AMD+analysis+first factor 0.09-0.10 s, 31 PARDISO numeric refactors 0.38-0.42 s, 32 solves 0.16-0.17 s, element assembly 0.18 s, line search (50 energy evaluations plus max-step) 0.08 s. Symbolic analysis and AMD ordering are already computed once and reused (phase 22 refactor through a precomputed value-source map); the iteration count (32, barrier-bound: most steps are 0.8 x alphaMax) is set by the convergence test and cannot change without changing the output. Tried and dropped: OpenMP blocktime 200 ms for the Newton loop (no gain on refactor/solve, slower assembly). Floor: the linear algebra alone is ~0.64 s at the fixed MKL thread count, so 100 ms is not reachable with byte-identical output.

Not exercised by the pipeline (fail to load on master and here, same failure): sphere_random, fandisk, Hand-tri-30k, crawfish. Botijo final state, 3 more runs: 1.952/2.814/1.711 s (median 1.952, machine loaded), every run screenshot sha 22e54fa9 = master; the interleaved A/B (master 1.888 vs 1.586 s median) remains the like-for-like number. [TMP] timing removed.

Buddha re-measure (coordinator, interleaved A/B under jvm.lock, master side = clean 0f52d26f worktree craw-68, busy machine): global grid map master 25.267/15.327/22.086 s (median 22.09 s), craw-72 17.529/13.299/16.735 s (median 16.74 s), about 24% faster. All six screenshots sha256 f8d8f9086ee8, identical. The earlier single-sample 18.29 -> 20.73 s slowdown was noise.

Round 2 step 1 (scaling measurement, temporary [TMP] per-iteration logging in NewtonRelaxation/PardisoCholesky/QuadLayoutEngine, worktree at 644ac7c5, one run each under jvm.lock). botijo: stage 1.485 s = assembly 0.37 + relax 0.96 + extraction 0.16; Newton n=43,614 free unknowns, nnzA(upper)=325k, PARDISO nnzL=2.32M (53/unknown), factor memory 25 MB; 32 iterations, 26 capped at 0.8 x alphaMax, 50 line-search energy evaluations in total (1-4 per iteration); Newton wall 848 ms = refactor 472 + solve 145 + assembly 169 + line search 55 (max-step 38); per iteration refactor ~12 ms, solve ~4.5 ms, assembly ~2.7 ms; peak heap 1.1 GB. Energy 1.06e6 after it 0 -> 4.2151e4; it 24 is already within 0.37% of the final energy (|g| 5.1e9 -> 2.7e4), the last 8 iterations buy 0.37%. buddha: stage 17.93 s = assembly 1.52 + relax 16.04 + extraction 0.37; n=279,444 (6.4x), nnzA=2.09M (6.4x), nnzL=17.3M (7.5x, 62/unknown), factor memory 164 MB, symbolic peak 167 MB; 86 iterations (2.7x), 82 capped at 0.8 x alphaMax, 97 evaluations in total; Newton wall 15.35 s = refactor 10.64 + solve 2.65 + assembly 1.64 + line search 0.41; per iteration refactor 124 ms (8.4x botijo, first ones 210 ms), solve 31 ms (6.8x), assembly 19 ms (3.6x); peak heap 2.6 GB. Explanation of the superlinear cost (Newton 18x for 6.4x unknowns): 2.7x more iterations x ~6.7x per-iteration cost. The per-iteration part is close to linear (fill per unknown only 53 -> 62, factor bandwidth-bound once its 164 MB leaves cache, ~1.3x over linear); line search is not a factor (1.1 evaluations per iteration); memory is not a factor; the single-threaded parts (assembly is pooled, max-step pooled) are small. The iteration count is the superlinear term: 95% of buddha's iterations are barrier-capped at 0.8 x alphaMax, so the step length is set by the single worst near-degenerate triangle anywhere in the mesh, and a mesh with 6.4x the triangles and a start 2x more distorted per triangle (energy 2.08e6 at start vs 6.29e4 final, 33x, against botijo's 29x) keeps hitting a new blocking triangle. Suite-wide on master the iteration count tracks start distortion: feline 3.85e6 -> 3.39e4 takes 74 iterations, block 1.17e5 -> 6.83e4 takes 16.

Round 2 step 2 (boundary check): the grid-map energy does NOT keep boundary vertices pinned. GridMapAssembly.assembleInitial (GridMapAssembly.java:148-151) builds the DOF system with seamCouplingPinned=false and nodeFreedomPinned=false. GridMapDofSystem.pinnedCopyVertices (GridMapDofSystem.java:369-396) then pins only critical/border nodes, fan-failed or holonomy-pinned nodes, one-sided arcs and seam arcs that cannot be coupled; every other arc vertex gets ONE slot shared by both patches (lines 173-195), read into the right patch through the seam transition when the arc is a seam (lines 154-172), and regular nodes are freed through their fan transforms (freedNodeFans). No constraint keeps a freed vertex on its arc's iso-line: DofSystem carries only a frozen mask, and the energy (SymmetricDirichletEnergy over every gathered triangle) has no penalty for leaving it. Measured: [grid-dof] pinnedVertices=72 on botijo (22,127 slots) and on buddha (140,002 slots) = exactly the singularities; coupledSeamArcs 227/706, freedNodes 374/2428. So arc vertices slide freely in 2D, along and across their arcs and across patches (worstMove 6.9 on botijo, 20.0 grid units on buddha), the problem is one connected map pinned only at the singularities, and it does not split exactly per patch: per-patch solves need an interface solve.

Round 2 step 3 (per-patch parallel solve + interface solve), first cut, uncommitted in the worktree: GridMapOptimizer.build now runs relaxPatchInteriors before the global Newton. Every slot referenced by one patch's triangles only (and not frozen) is that patch's interior; each patch is solved as its own NewtonRelaxation (patch-local DofSystem, its own flip-free line search through maximumStepOfRange, its own composite-majorized assembly) with every shared arc/node slot held, patches distributed dynamically (largest first) over the existing grid-optimize worker pool, each worker capped to one MKL thread through the new CholeskyBackend.limitCallingThreadSolverThreads (MKL_Set_Num_Threads_Local). Patches own disjoint slots, so the concurrent write-back is race-free. The existing global Newton then acts as the interface solve (it frees arcs and nodes as before). One run each: botijo patch phase 454 patches, 2802 patch iterations (max 15), 0.19 s, energy 1.208e6 -> 8.27e4; global Newton 32 -> 14 iterations (447 vs 848 ms); final energy 4.2153e4 vs master 4.21515e4 (+0.004%); stage 1.485 -> 1.170 s. buddha: patch phase 2498 patches, 15936 iterations (max 28), 0.62 s, energy 2.08e6 -> 2.75e5; global 86 -> 39 iterations (7.0 vs 15.35 s); final energy 6.2916e4 vs 6.2917e4; stage 17.93 -> 9.78 s; flipped 0 on both. Diagnosis of the remaining global iterations (temporary scan, removed): 37/39 are still capped at 0.8 x alphaMax, and the triangles within 2x of alphaMax are 1-14 interface triangles (a corner on a shared arc/node slot) per iteration, interior 0-3; the few blocking triangles sit on the arcs the global solve slides up to 20 grid units. Tried and dropped: PARDISO's own parallel nested dissection (iparm[1]=3) instead of the Java AMD order: nnzL 17.3M -> 15.8M, refactor time unchanged, solve 1.18 -> 0.66 s on buddha, not worth the shared-file change. Note: buddha's upstream input is not bit-stable run to run (280k unknowns 279444 vs 279450 in two runs), so its energies differ in the 5th digit between runs.

Round 2 step 3 finished. The per-patch solve moved into its own gridmap class PatchInteriorSolve (one patch's interior as a Newton system: patch-local slot numbering, frozen mask, Hessian pattern and composite-majorized assembly; it implements NewtonRelaxation.SystemAssembler and reuses GridMapOptimizer's element primitives cornerPosition/rotateElementToSlots/energyOfTriangleRange/maximumStepOfRange, made public along with the gathered-triangle arrays and KEY_ROW_SHIFT); the patch dispatch is inlined in GridMapOptimizer.build, so the SingleCallerHelper reports are gone; mvn -q compile clean. Output unchanged by the move. Interleaved A/B, medians of 3 (master = craw-68 at 0f52d26f, same session): botijo master 1.733 s (2.060/1.733/1.519) -> 1.234 s (1.369/1.234/1.194), 1.40x; buddha master 16.803 s (16.803/16.729/16.844) -> 8.194 s (8.242/8.122/8.194), 2.05x. Iterations: botijo patch phase 454 patches 2802 iterations (max 15) 0.17-0.20 s, global 32 -> 14; buddha 2498 patches 15936 iterations (max 28) 0.46-0.49 s, global 86 -> 39. Final energy botijo 4.2153e4 vs master 4.2151e4 (+0.005%), buddha 6.2916e4 vs 6.2917e4; flipped 0 on both. Worktree screenshots are stable run to run but differ from master's, as expected for round 2.

Round 2 step 4, both parts measured and dropped (no code kept). (a) Better flip-free start: symmetrized Floater mean-value weights (Floater 2003, positive on any valid 1-ring, so Tutte's fold-free guarantee holds) in place of the cotangent weights in PatchRectangleMap.build, computed on the patch's 3D triangles (the map's inputs; F is close to conformal to them, so the angles F would give differ little). Start energy fell a lot (botijo 1.208e6 -> 9.72e4, buddha 2.08e6 -> 4.34e5: the cotangent start carried a few badly shaped triangles), but the patch phase ends at the same energy to six digits (8.2674e4, 2.7486e5) with the same work (botijo 2802 -> 2837 patch iterations, max 15 -> 12, 0.17 -> 0.15 s; buddha 15936 -> 16191, max 28 -> 26, 0.46 -> 0.49 s) and the global solve takes as long (botijo 14 -> 14 iterations, buddha 39 -> 42): the per-patch Newton removes whatever the start's interior carried, and what is left is the interfaces, which the start does not touch. Stage botijo 1.196 s, buddha 8.405 s, single runs: no gain, reverted. (b) BCQN characteristic-gradient-norm stop (Zhu, Bridson, Kaufman 2018, Sec. 6: stop when ||grad E||_2 <= eps * <W> * ||l||_2, <W> = ||Hess W(I)||_2 = 8 for the symmetric Dirichlet density |F|^2+|F^-1|^2, l_i = one-ring perimeter in the reference, computed per slot from the gradient operator as 2A|grad lambda_i|): characteristic norm 8||l|| = 5.07e3 on botijo, 6.45e3 on buddha. With the paper's eps=1e-3 (thresholds 5.1 / 6.5) it never fires: the smallest gradient norm the global solve reaches is 12.6 (botijo) and 25.6 (buddha), so the existing relative-energy stall test (three iterations under 1e-4) always stops first. A looser eps is not safe: buddha's gradient drops to 48.5 at iteration 31 while the energy is still 1.3% above its final value (barrier-capped steps keep descending), so eps=7.5e-3 would break the 0.5% rule; eps=5e-3 would save about 4 iterations on each mesh, but the margin between that and a regression is under 2x, so it is a tuned threshold, not a mesh-independent one. Combining it with one stall instead of three saves 2 iterations on botijo (~30 ms) and none on buddha. Dropped. Round 2 therefore keeps step 3 only.

Worst energy change +0.0038% (limit 0.5%), every map flip-free. The uv deviation is largest where the energy is flattest along the arcs (buddha's arcs slide up to 20 units in both paths): both paths stop at the same energy to 4-5 digits but at slightly different points of a flat valley.
